title: Gamma Radiation of Drosophila suzukii Under Hypoxia and Normoxia Conditions
author: Fabiana Sassu
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.76whrfe

steps.title: Prepare pupae on moist paper
steps.instruction: Two days before adult emergence, carefully separate D. suzukii pupae from the larval medium and place them on moist paper to prevent drying while they complete maturation; in this experiment use a total of 6000 pupae (2000 for each atmosphere treatment and 2000 non‑irradiated controls).

steps.title: Select correctly aged pupae
steps.instruction: Choose pupae that are exactly five days post‑pupation (dark brown with visible red eyes and wings) which are about 24 h before adult emergence; this age window is critical for sterility outcomes.

steps.title: Apply hypoxia and normoxia pre‑treatments
steps.instruction: Six hours before irradiation, treat the selected pupae under two atmospheric conditions:

substeps.instruction: Hypoxia: place the required number of pupae in a polyethylene bag (VWR Polyethylene Tubing 89071‑044, Radnor, PA), seal with a tabletop sealer (Rische + Herfurth GMBH, Polystar 244, Hamburg, Germany), tie tightly to minimise excess air and avoid overcrowding; incubate the bag for 5 h at 18 °C to allow metabolic consumption of O₂; verify oxygen depletion with a CheckMate3 gas‑sensor (Dansensor A/S, Ringsted, Denmark) – final O₂ ≈ 0.3 %.
Normoxia: keep the second group of ≈2000 pupae in normal laboratory conditions (ambient O₂ ≈ 20.9 %) at 22 °C for the same 5‑hour period.

steps.title: Expose pupae to gamma radiation
steps.instruction: Transfer the hypoxia‑treated pupae (still sealed in their bags) and the normoxia‑treated pupae (placed in perforated bags allowing airflow) together to the middle of a 60 Co irradiator (Gamma Cell‑220, Nordion, Canada) so all receive the same dose; irradiate simultaneously with three 10 mm × 10 mm Gafchromic® HD‑V2 dosimetry films (International Specialty Products, NJ, USA).

substeps.instruction: After irradiation, measure the optical density of the films 24 h later using a Radiochromic reader (FWT‑92D, Far West Technology, Inc., Goleta, CA, USA).
Remove pupae from their bags and place each atmospheric group into separate cages (17 cm × 8 cm × 11.5 cm) for adult emergence.
Maintain a third group of non‑irradiated pupae under standard laboratory conditions as a control.

steps.title: Select emerged adults for experiments
steps.instruction: Allow pupae to emerge; use only adults that emerge within 24 h after irradiation, sex them under a brief CO₂ anesthesia, and keep them for downstream crosses.

steps.title: Set up mating crosses
steps.instruction: Establish three types of crosses for each radiation dose, each replicated five times: (1) irradiated females × non‑irradiated males, (2) non‑irradiated females × irradiated males, and (3) non‑irradiated females × non‑irradiated males (control).

steps.title: Maintain adults for sexual maturation
steps.instruction: Keep each cross together for four days to ensure sexual maturation and insemination; provide water and a food mixture of sugar and hydrolysate enzymatic yeast (MP Biomedicals) in a 3:1 ratio.

steps.title: Collect eggs from oviposition
steps.instruction: On the fifth day, place three fresh blueberries in each cage as oviposition sites; replace blueberries daily and collect eggs with forceps until 500 eggs are obtained per replicate, per cross, per dose, or for a maximum of three days.

steps.title: Incubate eggs and calculate metrics
steps.instruction: Transfer collected eggs onto a wet black net in a Petri dish containing larval diet; count eggs and later count hatched larvae. Compute fecundity as (total eggs per cage ÷ average eggs of control cross) and fertility as (eggs hatched ÷ eggs laid).
